transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 16:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO, Coral Analytics), Benji Cho (Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on Coral's plan to roll out multi-tenant user-facing assistants across several product lines. Main seams: whether they go Hosted first versus a Dedicated pool or full Private (VPC/onprem) later, how the edge-mux/gateway will talk to Redwood, and integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex style pipelines. They care about predictable latency, quota enforcement per-tenant, and end-to-end observability into token cost and tail latency.

Topics discussed:
- Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- SDK language support and LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors
- Gateway / proxy patterns (edge mux, sidecar vs central proxy)
- Rate limits / per-route quotas and burst policies
- Observability hooks: traces, structured logs, per-token cost breakdown
- Security: VPC, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, SOC2

Action items (quick):
- Lena to send Dedicated pricing + SLA
- Marcus to prepare benchmark plan and SDK snippets
- Benji to share production traffic profile

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Hi Marta, hi Benji, Samir — we appreciate you taking time. Marcus and I are Redwood's AE/SE pair for Coral. Today we want to understand your integration surface and constraints so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated, or Private path and show what the SDK + gateway pattern looks like.
[00:22] Marta Ruiz: Thanks Lena — quick context: Coral is putting conversational assistants in our analytics product and in support. Initial traffic target is small but we expect rapid growth — maybe 1k concurrent sessions by Q2. We need per-tenant isolation on quotas and billing, and strict audit logs for compliance.
[00:40] Marcus Chen: Got it. When you say "per-tenant quotas" do you mean "per-customer API keys, or per-internal-tenant concept?"
[00:47] Benji Cho: Per-customer, yes. Each customer should have a quota and soft limits, also we want burst for premium customers. We also want to limit max tokens per request and track cost back to the customer id.
[01:05] Marcus Chen: Cool. Two immediate levers we provide: token-level metering on requests and per-key rate limits. For Hosted, you can attach metadata (customer_id) to requests and get cost breakdowns in Console. For Dedicated/Private you get dedicated GPU pools and can enforce per-route quotas at your gateway or via our per-key throttles.
[01:25] Samir Khan: Wanted to check connectivity — for Private we'd need VPC peering and possibly onprem deployment in our colo. Any constraints on establishing a peering or using a transit gateway?
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: Yes, for Private we do customer-managed networking. We support VPC peering and Transit Gateway setups; Marcus can send the connectivity checklist. For onprem we'd package the control plane or run a private appliance — there are some options.
[01:49] Benji Cho: And KMS? We need to bring our keys and HSM integration.
[01:53] Marcus Chen: We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping and can support HSM-backed key stores. For Hosted customers we offer envelope encryption by default; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own KMS. There might be some ops work for HSM.
[02:08] Marta Ruiz: Good — SOC2 is onboarded but we also need logs for audits. Do you preserve detailed per-request logs?
[02:15] Marcus Chen: We have structured logs, request traces, and token-level cost breakdowns you can retain. Retention is configurable; for enterprise plans you can push logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.

[02:30] Lena Ortiz: I want to dig into how you plan to route traffic. Do you intend to put a gateway/edge-mux in front of Redwood, or call Redwood directly from app servers?
[02:40] Samir Khan: We're evaluating an edge-mux approach — one central proxy in our control plane that handles tenant routing, rate limiting, and auth. It then fans requests to the inference backends. We like a single ingress point.
[02:53] Marcus Chen: That's a common pattern. Two ways: 1) make the edge-mux act as a dumb proxy and let Redwood do per-key quotas and billing; 2) keep quota enforcement at the edge and use Redwood's SDK for batching/observability. Both are possible. If you want to retain full control over throttling, the edge-enforced approach is cleaner.
[03:15] Benji Cho: For batching we have short prompts — many 64–256 token requests, avg context 512. We worry about latency — can't go above 200ms p50 for a lot of user flows.
[03:28] Marcus Chen: Right — batching helps cost but can add latency. Our runtime supports continuous batching and latency SLOs; on Dedicated you can configure smaller batching windows to favor latency. Also prefix caching and KV cache reuse can cut tokens for repeated context.
[03:45] Marta Ruiz: You mention KV cache — we've seen "K-V cash" in another doc, what exactly is that?
[03:49] Marcus Chen: Sorry, K-V cache — it's the cached key/value states for decoder-only models to avoid recomputing prefix attention. It speeds up generation for long sessions. There are also prefix caches for repeated prompts.

[04:08] Lena Ortiz: Integration with LangChain and LlamaIndex — is that first-class?
[04:13] Marcus Chen: We have SDKs with adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex; the Python SDK has a connector class you can drop into a chain. Note some naming in older docs refers to "Lama index" — that's the same thing, just transcription noise.
[04:28] Benji Cho: We use LlamaIndex heavily in vector search flows. How are embeddings and rerank handled? Would we go to Redwood for embeddings and then host vector DB externally?
[04:37] Marcus Chen: You can do either: Redwood provides embeddings API (hosted) and you can store vectors in your DB (Pinecone, Milvus, etc.). For latency-sensitive rerank we recommend co-locating the vector DB near the inference endpoints or using our Dedicated capacity to reduce cross-network hops.

[04:55] Marta Ruiz: Security again — SSO and RBAC. Can we provision roles per Red Team?
[05:01] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support SAML/SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC with granular roles. Console and token-level scoping allow you to separate dev/test and prod keys.

[05:20] Samir Khan: About quotas and burst: we need per-tenant monthly quotas but also per-second limits to protect the pool. How do you handle burst for premium customers?
[05:30] Marcus Chen: We have per-key rate limits (requests/sec) and token-rate guards. For Dedicated you can configure burst buckets and guaranteed throughput for certain tenants. In Hosted we can set soft-burst policies but the Dedicated model gives you more predictable isolation.

[05:46] Benji Cho: Can we do per-route cost attribution? Like route X charges customer Y?
[05:50] Marcus Chen: Yes — you can attach metadata to requests (headers or SDK fields) and get cost attribution in the Console and via usage APIs. Many customers push that into billing pipelines.

[06:05] Lena Ortiz: Quick note on SDKs: we support Python, Node, and go-to-market has open-source connectors for LangChain. Marcus, can you walk the team through a sample SDK call?
[06:16] Marcus Chen: Sure, high level — here's the pattern: set an API key or use mTLS, attach customer_id in metadata, call client.generate({model, prompt, max_tokens, user: "customer:123"}) — the SDK will handle streaming, retry, and structured outputs. I'll paste examples after the call.
[06:37] Benji Cho: Retrying — do you provide idempotency keys?
[06:40] Marcus Chen: Yes, idempotency token optional on request to avoid double charge on retries. Also for streaming we give chunk ids.

[07:00] Marta Ruiz: Observability — we need traces and integration with Datadog. Can we get per-request traces and export them?
[07:06] Marcus Chen: Yes, we have distributed tracing hooks and you can forward traces to Datadog or Honeycomb. We also export structured JSON logs to S3 and have an events API for custom sinks.

[07:21] Samir Khan: If we go edge-mux + Redwood Hosted, are we losing anything around latency or observability?
[07:30] Marcus Chen: Slightly higher network hops, but if your edge-mux is in the same region it should be minimal. Observability remains intact — you can pass trace headers through the proxy and Redwood will propagate tracing. The main tradeoff is where you enforce quotas (edge vs provider).

[07:50] Benji Cho: For Dedicated, what's the onboarding timeline? We may need it in prod in ~8 weeks if possible.
[07:58] Lena Ortiz: For Dedicated, typical onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on capacity sizing and networking. We can accelerate with committed capacity and advance network prep. Marcus will outline the lift.

[08:10] Marcus Chen: On benchmarks: to recommend instance types and batch windows we'll need a sample prompt distribution and QPS shape. If you can give a 24-hour sample trace (anonymized) we can run a sizing sim and show expected latency/cost.
[08:24] Benji Cho: We'll pull a day of traces and token distribution. Also we use several long-context flows up to 4k tokens for analyst assistants — will that be an issue?
[08:34] Marcus Chen: We support long context, but cost and memory change. For long sequences we recommend model variants and quantization recommendations; Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization for Dedicated to cut cost while keeping quality.

[08:52] Marta Ruiz: Can you do canary deploys or A/B tests for model rollouts? We want to roll new models to a subset of users.
[08:59] Marcus Chen: Yes — our Console supports rollouts: canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can route a percentage of traffic to a new model and fall back if latency or quality regressions are detected.

[09:15] Lena Ortiz: Any hard blockers on your side for starting a Hosted pilot?
[09:20] Benji Cho: Mostly policy and egress constraints — some customers require data residency. For pilot we'd pick a non-sensitive tenant set and test Hosted. If pilot meets latency/observability needs, then we evaluate Dedicated for isolation.
[09:33] Marta Ruiz: About data residency — we need EU-only data for a chunk of customers. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning?
[09:40] Marcus Chen: We have region pinning in Hosted and Dedicated; Private is obviously fully local. For Hosted we can pin models to eu-west-1 and ensure data doesn't leave region. We'll include that in the checklist.

[09:55] Samir Khan: A couple quick clarifications on pricing model — do you charge embeddings separately and how are streaming tokens billed?
[10:02] Lena Ortiz: Embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; generation is per input+output tokens. Streaming doesn't change token accounting — it's about how tokens are delivered. We'll send a pricing breakdown.

[10:18] Benji Cho: Can you show how LangChain integration would look in our codebase? We use Python and have a custom retriever layer.
[10:25] Marcus Chen: We'll provide a LangChain adapter snippet that returns a retriever-compatible interface. The adapter will call Redwood's embed API for vectorization and generation for rerank. We'll include sample code after the call.

[10:40] Speaker 1: [unlabeled] I had a question about burst queues — if multiple tenants burst simultaneously, how do you avoid noisy neighbor?
[10:48] Marcus Chen: On Hosted we use soft fairness and admission policies; on Dedicated you can reserve guaranteed throughput and enforce strict per-tenant caps to prevent noisy neighbor. Also, routing policies can spill to a fallback model to keep latency.

[11:05] Marta Ruiz: For audit and compliance we need immutable logs and export to our S3 with lifecycle rules. Is that supported?
[11:12] Marcus Chen: Yes — enterprise plans support pushing raw logs to S3 with immutability options and we can sign BAA/NDA if needed.

[11:25] Lena Ortiz: Great — sounds like next steps are: we'll send the connectivity checklist, Dedicated pricing, and a short SDK/LangChain quickstart. Marcus will schedule a deep-dive for benchmarks once you provide traces.
[11:38] Benji Cho: Sounds good. One more — do you support client-side encryption for payloads in transit?
[11:44] Marcus Chen: TLS is standard. For extra lane we support client-side encryption and token-splitting workflows in Private deployments. For Hosted it's less common but we can discuss envelope encryption with KMS.

[11:58] Marta Ruiz: Excellent, thanks. We'll collect the traffic sample and follow up on dates for the benchmark session.
[12:06] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all. We'll email notes and the checklist. Marcus, any final items?
[12:11] Marcus Chen: I'll add the SDK examples, a sample LangChain adapter, and the benchmark runbook to the shared drive. Expect those by 10/26.
[12:20] Meeting end.
